entries.subject: The colour of the photosphere
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at the published 4,300 K (Donati et al. 2012), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer into sRGB with the D65 white.

entries.subject: A Gaia BP/RP spectrum of this star as the colour
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 has no BP/RP spectrum that describes this star alone, so the paper temperature gives the colour.
entries.revisitWhen: Gaia publishes a spectrum of this star alone.

entries.subject: Limb darkening of the sphere
entries.finding: No fit of this star's limb exists, so the sphere is darkened by the quadratic Johnson V law Claret and Bloemen (2011) compute from ATLAS model atmospheres at 4,300 K and log g 4.0, from the record's mass and radius: a model. It replaced the uniform disc of the first version.

entries.subject: GQ Lup A's own disc
entries.finding: The star's compact dust disc is imaged by ALMA (MacGregor et al. 2017; Wu et al. 2017) and a spiral arm in scattered light (Stolker et al. 2021), but no package of it is built here.
entries.revisitWhen: A disc package is scoped for this system.
